name: Badr al-Dīn Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr ibn ʿUmar al-Makhzūmī al-Damāmīnī
summary: Alexandrian grammarian and judge who ended his life in India; his commentaries on Ibn Mālik's al-Tashīl and Ibn Hishām's Mughnī carried Egyptian grammar to the Deccan.
bio: Ibn al-Damāmīnī was born in Alexandria in 763/1362, taught there and in Cairo, and served as a judge. Debts and misfortune, the sources say, sent him travelling: to Yemen, where he taught in Zabīd, and in 820/1417 to India, first to Gujarat and then to the Bahmanī court of Gulbarga in the Deccan, where he died in 827/1424.

His Taʿlīq al-farāʾid comments on Ibn Mālik's al-Tashīl; his commentary on Ibn Hishām's Mughnī, finished in India, criticised Ibn Hishām so often that al-Shumunnī wrote al-Munṣif to answer him. He also wrote on prosody (al-ʿUyūn al-ghāmiza) and commented on al-Bukhārī.
